root_causes.description: The cart service shows a sustained, elevated container memory working set (~93MB mean, ~108MB max across the window) relative to comparable Go-based services (shipping ~12.5MB, checkout ~24.7MB), with normal CPU and zero error rate. The memory pressure coincides with a container recreation, consistent with an injected memory-stress fault on the cart pods.

evidence.expected_baseline: ~12-25MB for comparable Go services (shipping mean=12480512, checkout mean=24669661)
cart mean=93337463 B, i.e. ~7x elevation versus shipping

evidence.observed_value: cart container created twice within the window, indicating a pod restart
evidence.expected_baseline: count=1 for a stable, non-restarted pod
p99 ~4-12ms for cart at steady state

root_causes.description: A cart pod container was recreated (restart count increased ~1 over the window; container Created/Started events observed twice). This is consistent with memory-pressure-induced restart, though no explicit OOMKilled event was captured in the lookback.

evidence.observed_value: cart container started twice within the window

root_causes.description: cart server-side p99 latency shows a transient spike (up to ~78ms vs ~4ms median) early in the window. This is likely a secondary symptom of memory pressure rather than the primary fault, as error rate and CPU remained normal.

evidence.observed_value: mean=1.116 req/s, max=1.267 req/s (stable throughput, no saturation)

remediation_steps: Increase the memory limit/request for the cart deployment to relieve memory pressure and prevent OOM-induced restarts.
Roll/restart the cart pods to clear the memory-stressed container and restore a clean working set.
Inspect cart pods for an injected memory stressor (e.g., stress-ng sidecar/ephemeral container) and remove it.
Add/alert on container_memory_working_set_bytes and OOMKilled events for cart to detect memory_stress faults early.
Verify cart p99 latency and restart counts return to baseline (~<15ms, 0 restarts) after remediation.
